newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products - fuel tumbles, light ends steady.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products - fuel tumbles, light ends steady.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were weaker on Friday with the exception of gasoline and naphtha.

Gasoline was steady to slightly higher with demand for premium unleaded surfacing from Ukraine, ex-Yugoslovian countries and eastern Mediterranean destinations, a trader said. Lebanon, Turkey, Greece and ex-Yugoslovian countries were in the market for low octane gasoline, she said. A regular unleaded Romanian cargo and a premium unleaded Israeli cargo were seen on offer, she said.
"We seem balanced now on 95 unleaded," she said.
Naphtha was steady to higher but traders said physical action was quiet with Oct business completed.
In gas oil, low sulphur diesel was down $2 at around Nov IPE +$18 offered. Buying interest was meagre. Russian was offered at Nov IPE +2, up to $1 firmer.
Traders said Turkey awarded five cargoes of Turkish 0.5 percent sulphur heating oil totalling 125,000 tonnes to 130,000 tonnes of imports.
One cargo went to Nova and another to Galaxy for delivery Nov 5-9. Three cargoes went to Tempotrade for delivery Nov 10-15, they said. Turkey had asked for two cargoes.

High sulphur cracked fuel was knocked sharply lower with a trade done at $107.25 fob Med. Dealers said the price was very aggressive shaving dollars off an already buffeted price. Some suggested the deal was designed for pricing purposes on cargoes over the weekend and that the market would regain $110 and more next week.
Low sulphur cracked fuel was slow and looking $1 easier at $130-131 cif Med amid good supply. The main Med buyer appeared quiet today, but was expected to be more active next week.
